newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Further EU fish catch cuts expected in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Further EU fish catch cuts expected in 1997.

text.p: The European Commission is expected on Friday to propose further sharp cuts in fish catches next year to protect threatened stocks.

European Commission sources said that EU and international scientists have warned that major reductions will be needed in catches of mackerel and North Sea herring as well as plaice and sole in order to rebuild seriously depleted supplies.
"More cuts are essential," said one source, adding that the reductions were in line with plans to reduce fishing capacity in coming years to match the decline in fish stocks.
The proposal will be discussed by EU fisheries ministers on December 19-20.
Each year fisheries ministers ease the cuts in order to head off strong protests from the fishing industry.
The EU executive has vainly argued that such action is shortsighted as it results in a deterioration of stocks and threatens the long-term survival of the fishing industry.
The proposal sets total allowable catches (TACs) for different types of fish in each fishing zone. Catches of North Sea sole would be halved to 12,000 tonnes.
In some areas, fish stocks are jointly managed with non-EU countries, notably with Norway in the North Sea, and have to be shared.
The balance is then allocated between EU member states according to a pre-set key.

However the Commission will be unable to propose any TACs for several important North Sea stocks, including cod and haddock, because negotiations with Norway on 1997 catch levels are still continuing.
